title: The Same Boat
logline: A fisherman's boat has been repaired so many times that no original plank is left, but everyone still calls it by the same name.
human_question: If every part has changed, what is it that stays 'the same'?

premise.story: A boat's repair season told through the fisherman, the carpenter and the boat's history.
premise.place: A fishing beach or lagoon where boats are hauled up and mended.
premise.experience: Salt, wood, tar and the sea: an old vessel made new again.

concept_links.why: The conventional 'same boat' against its ever-changing parts.
Analysing a whole into constituents, the method the series later turns on the self.
A collective concept that survives total replacement of its parts.

what_camera_could_observe: Old planks removed, new ones shaped
The boat's name painted or repainted
The fisherman's memories of the boat
what_must_be_real: The boat's actual repair history, as told by its owners.

possible_arc.turn: Plank by plank, the old boat disappears.
possible_arc.ending_open: The 'same' boat goes back to sea.

suggestions.name: Negombo lagoon (oruwa outrigger canoes)
suggestions.why: Traditional outrigger boats still built and repaired.
suggestions.verify: Access, permissions and current conditions are unverified.

suggestions.why: Beach-hauled boats and a strong fishing community.
